I can e-mail you some pictures if you would like or the curling brush and my burnt wrist. My husband was in the bathroom when this happened and he couldn't believe it fired up like that.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn on the user's wrist, indicating a moderate level of severity. The occurrence likelihood is considered possible given that a single incident occurred, but there's no information suggesting it happens frequently.

incident_description: My wife was using a Conair Ionic Cord Keeper 1875 Hair Dryer model 169P date code 0507S when the cord caught on fire just past the rigid part of the cord where the warning tags are affixed.  The flames shot out several inches, and fortunatelu I can say that it was plugged in along a granite backsplash and not drywall, I do believe it could have caught fire.  The house breaker and the GFI did not trip that it was plugged into.  Looking at it now, this can not be the only tim ethis has happened.  Looking at the design, the cord spools back into the hairdryer and it it is at this point where the cord probally became weak and probally cracked, eventually caussing the failure.  I called Conair, they just stated that it was out of warranty and I could write to the corporate office.  I did one better and called, the gave me the phone number of [REDACTED] [REDACTED], I have called 5 times, left 2 messages, none have been returned.  I would think at minimum they would be interested in seeing the hairdryer and damage that occured, only a scare to my wife, but I did take pictures of the backsplash before cleaning it off.
justification: The incident involved a cord fire but fortunately resulted in no injury. The design of the product may have contributed to the failure, suggesting a possible rather than isolated issue.

incident_description:
I was drying my hair with my Conair IONSHINE  hairdryer when suddenly a bright blue-white flame about 4"-5" long shot noisily out of the place where the cord met the plug. It burned for a few seconds, and then the cord fell off the plug, at which time the flames stopped. I unplugged the plug from the socket. It looks like the cord melted at the attachment point. Black residue is all around the wall outlet and on the sink below.

I called the Conair Hotline, but they said they couldn't do anything because the dryer, based on model and serial number, is out of warranty. The warranty is for two years, but I only bought it 10 or so months ago. I was told that unless I had my receipt, (I do not), they couldn't help me. 

I can understand not replacing it if the motor died or no longer blew hot air. I know hair dryers don't last forever. But this is a safety issue, and I think they should replace it for me, although I'm not really sure I want another one of their products now.
justification: The incident involved a hairdryer with a faulty cord and plug connection that caused a flame, but no injury was reported. The likelihood of such an event is unlikely as it seems to be an isolated malfunction.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she accidentally sprayed some of the contents from the pepper spray and it caused her throat to close up, she went to the [redacted] and was released, she was advised that the product was suppose to react in that manner, she eventually recuperated that day but suffered aftereffects, adverse health problems. Consumer added: After incident I am experiencing memory loss and I have coughing spells now and throat problems and headaches.  I was scared to death almost when my throat closed up. 

8/21/11 Consumer stated that she returned the product to the store.

Consumer feels that this product's potency is enough to kill wild beasts, seniors should not purchase.  Is not clear on instructions re: how to use it. It is unsafe and should not be sold.
justification: The consumer suffered an injury from the pepper spray, experiencing throat closure, and subsequent health problems including memory loss, coughing spells, and headaches. The incident was not fatal, but the consumer required medical attention and experienced lasting effects.

incident_description: I left the conair EURO 1600 blowdryer plugged in but off. It was left in this state for a few weeks. This morning the blow dryer turned on (in the off position) at full blast.  It was overheating and would have caused a fire had we not immediately heard it and turned it off. Everything smelled like burnt plastic.
justification: The blowdryer malfunctioned and overheated but was turned off before causing a fire or injury. The incident was caught immediately, preventing harm.

incident_description: On 9/5/11 I was using this brush & when I turned it off as I was moving it away from my face, there was a loud pop and sparks flew out of the brush, one spark burning a hole in my nightgown. The other sparks I put out on the floor. If this had still been near my face, it might have caused major damage to my skin or eyes. Or if had been wearing something else, it could have caught fire. The day this happened, I also notice the heat seemed to be not working well on the high setting but working just fine on the low setting which is the main setting I use. I did report this to Revlon through their web site.
justification: The incident resulted in a burn through the nightgown, indicating an injury, and the user had previously noticed declining quality of the product and malfunctioning heat settings. However, the injury was minor and the product had previously functioned normally for years.

incident_description: The handle for holding the hair dryer gets very hot using it on the Warm High setting, and quickly becomes too hot to touch. It's hottest at the part where my pointer finger holds the handle, right over the seam joining the purple and silver parts of the dryer. I purchased the hair dryer at Bed Bath and Beyond within the past several months so it is not an old hair dryer. The hair dryer started becoming hot like this within the past few weeks and started with the hot-to-the-touch taking longer to build up than occurred the past two day, at which time, it became too hot to hold within 5 minutes. The hair dryer information is as follows: Revlon 1875 Ionic Ceramic; Model RV484, 1875W 125VAC 60Hz.
justification: The hair dryer handle becomes too hot to touch, indicating a potential burn hazard, but no injury was reported. The issue developed over time, suggesting a possible design or manufacturing flaw.

incident_description:
Consumer stated that she had plugged in the hair straightener for approximately 1 min and when the light turned red indicating that it was ready to use she took it up and was about to use it in her hair when it emitted a large spark and then it went out.

Consumer stated that she had contacted the manufacturer and returned a few of them before because of similar problems.

incident_description: Wife recently purchased a Conair Curling Iron Model M120.  Using it yesterday, she brushed it up against her cheek and received a significant electrical shock.  I examined the unit this morning and found that the cord insulation is cracked exposing both electical conductors where the cord enters the swivel mount for the cord. Photos of the device and the cracked cord are available as is the device itself.

incident_description: Purchased the Prosepra Electronic Pulse Massager, P-1-N43B250-B000XHNBLO from amazon.com; when received and began using, the electrical impulses were so severe and high as to be sever and painful, causing muscles and limbs to spasm wildly. Hope to spare others, whether this was a defective model and they are all like this.  It is more like a torture device.

The likelihood of such an occurrence is unlikely as the user has experience with similar devices and suggests this may have been a defective model.

incident_description:
Using a "Remington All That !" hair dryer it began making a rattling sound and loud exploding
sounds.  It smoked and had an electrical wire burning smell.  Had to turn off the hair dryer as
the GFI and the plug did not activate.  There are part rattling around inside.  There were no
injuries, put the product seem very dangerous.
justification: The incident involved a malfunctioning hair dryer with smoke and a burning smell, but no injuries occurred. The product's condition suggests a potential for danger, but the lack of injury in this instance leads to a severity level of 2.

incident_description: I have had this for a little over a year and wanted to report from day one and never knew how.. It works fine with dry hair but you can use it with wet hair it does not in any way and it needs to warn that the steam from it with wet hair will burn you hands,neck ,face ect. I used it on wet hair and was scalded by the steam!
justification: The user reported being scalded by steam when using the product on wet hair, indicating an injury occurred. The likelihood of this occurrence is unlikely as the user did not expect this outcome despite it being a foreseeable risk.

incident_description: I purchased a Conair massage wand unit that evidently has a heating device in it.  The switch to the heating device is not labled very well, and is not a switch, but a piece you turn on the wand.It looks like it is just part of the handle.  I never even knew the device was capable of heat.  The switch was turned on by accident, and must have been faulty for it became so hot as to give me a second and third degree burn on my leg.
justification: The incident resulted in a second and third degree burn, indicating a moderate to severe injury. The likelihood of this occurrence is unlikely as it was an accidental activation of a poorly labeled device.

incident_description:
I had been drying my hair and turned the hair dryer off and hung it in the towel rack next to me.  I continued to get ready for the day in the bathroom where the hairdryer was.  I heard a loud "pop" sound in the direction of the hairdryer.  I looked toward the sound to see smoke and flames coming out the handle of my hairdryer.  I quickly unplugged it and carried it by the far end of the cord to outside.  I had this hairdryer for several years. The switch seemed to be touchy or sensitive.  When I would turn the switch on sometimes the hair dryer would not turn on immediately.  
I reported the incident to Conair since it was one of their products.  I was told that since it had been greater than two years since the purchase of the hair dryer they would not replace it.  The person on the phone asked to make sure that I didn't sustain any injury, which I did not.  I told the company representative that it wasn't a free replacement that I was looking for but to protect others who may use the same hair dryer.  I discussed with her my concern that if someone left the product plugged in and then left his or her home the product could catch fire and cause serious damage to someone or his or her home. She said she would pass my concern on to the marketing division.    This was the end of our conversation.  I reported this to the company in July of this year 2011.

The product is a Conair Ion Shine 1875 hair dryer

incident_description: While blow-drying my 6-year-old daughter's hair, the hair dryer shot a long spark (approx. 4 inches) from the bottom of the hair dryer. At the time, I had the hair dryer directly in front of her face, drying her bangs. Luckily, my child was not injured. The breaker on the plug did not trip, the dryer continued to run.  I immediately turned it off and unplugged it.  Upon examining the blow dryer, I noticed the cord was worn and the electrical cord wires were exposed. This happened at the base of the hair dryer where the cord protector ends (the rubber piece that keeps the electrical cord from bending too far). The rubber piece is hard rubber causing it to wear through the electrical cord. The hair dryer was purchased on 8/31/2010 at Sally Beauty Supply and is a GVP Pro Model # 264880. The hair dryer is still in my possession.
justification: The incident involved a hair dryer shooting a spark, but luckily, no injury occurred. The worn cord with exposed wires suggests a potential for future incidents.

incident_description: RE: Mack's AquaBlock Earplugs.  On March 3, 2011, I used these earplugs for swimming, as advertised on the box of the product. These plugs are made especially for water use to "help prevent swimmer's ear." When I inserted the plugs into my ears as instructed on the box, the plug for my left ear slipped down the ear canal and was impossible to get out with my fingers. I had to go to the emergency room at the local hospital in Bellingham, WA. There was a lot of pressure and increasing pain during this incident. Though I went to the hospital immediately after this happened, I waited approximately 2 hours and 45 minutes with the plug in my ear before the doctor could see me to get it out. He took a long needle, bent it into a kind of hook and had to literally fish it out of my ear. The doctor was shocked to learn that the earplug was designed for water sports and for adults, as the plug is too thin to insert safely into an adult ear. This incident created a huge trauma for me as well as an emergency room visit cost I have not yet been billed for.
justification: The incident resulted in an injury requiring medical intervention, as the earplug caused discomfort, pressure, and pain, and had to be removed by a doctor using a needle. The likelihood of such an occurrence is unlikely, given that the product is designed for water sports and adults, but the design flaw led to this specific incident.
